ceiling_directive: Add a feasible finite-sample RankPeel theorem that estimates the queried Jacobian ranks under primitive smoothness, density, and singular-value-margin conditions, with a uniform exact-adjacency recovery probability and end-to-end polynomial runtime.
improvement_directive: Replace the population-only rank and version-stability oracle with estimable rank statistics, and prove uniform finite-sample recovery of the same layered adjacency target under explicit primitive regularity and rank-gap conditions.
critique: The note proves exact RankPeel recovery only on query-regular or positive-density strict subclasses; on the unchanged Prashant–Ng–Zhang–Huang class it instead proves that the proposed law-level rank oracle can be undefined and the algorithm can abort. Since the anchor already identifies the same full adjacency target and already uses pure-descendant surrogates, the delivered advance is a quadratic population-oracle schedule, a restricted separator argument, and a version-instability correction rather than a new full-class identification result. The claimed complexity treats membership in the version-stability domain and exact Jacobian rank evaluation as unit-cost oracle calls, supplies no optimality lower bound against competing query protocols, and gives no finite-sample method or recovery guarantee. The framing accurately limits recovery to the strict subclasses, but the closest-literature comparison does not establish quantitatively how much the quadratic schedule improves the anchor's construction, leaving the practical and methodological significance below the field-tier floor. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.6 < 7.2, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
